name: Sami Al Majanini
role: Biomedical Engineer · Researcher in EEG Signal Processing & Mechanistic Interpretability
statement: I build geometry-aware models of EEG and open up the networks that learn from it. My work connects Riemannian methods on covariance manifolds, graph learning for neurological disease detection, and causal interpretability of EEG foundation models and large language models.
photoAlt: Sami Al Majanini in a dark green suit at the 8th International Conference on Advances in Biomedical Engineering (ICABME 2025)
about: My graduate training is an MSc in Internet of Things & Smart Systems Engineering at the Lebanese University. My research spans EEG signal processing, Riemannian geometry on SPD manifolds, graph learning for neurological disease detection, and mechanistic interpretability, including Theory of Mind in large language models and EEG foundation models.

I am drawn to questions that sit between signal and mechanism: what structure does a brain recording actually carry, and what does a model learn to do with it? interests.title: EEG & Brain Signals
interests.text: Preprocessing, source-space analysis and robust decoding of noisy, non-stationary neural recordings.

interests.title: Riemannian Geometry
interests.text: Covariance matrices as points on SPD manifolds: geodesic distances, tangent-space features and geometry-aware learning.

interests.title: Graph Neural Networks for Neuro
interests.text: Connectivity-aware models that detect neurological disease, such as Alzheimer's, from source-space EEG graphs.

interests.title: Mechanistic Interpretability
interests.text: Activation patching and causal analysis to show how LLMs encode beliefs and how EEG foundation models represent brain activity.
